phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve
one more problem.
Now let us first read the question. A train crosses a one hundred fifty meter platform in twenty seconds and a two hundred fifty meter platform in twenty-five seconds.
We need to find the speed of the train.
Given
platform one length equals one hundred fifty meters.
Time to cross platform one equals twenty seconds.
Platform two length equals two hundred fifty meter.
Time to cross platform two equals twenty-five seconds.
Let
length of the train equals L meter.
Speed of the train
equals
S meter per second.
Now,
when a train crosses a platform, it does not cover only the platform.
The entire train has to enter the platform, and then the last coach has to come out.
So the total distance covered is distance equals length of train plus length of platform.
So distance equals L plus one hundred fifty. Also, we know speed equals distance divided by time.
Now for the first platform,
time taken equals twenty, so S equals L plus one hundred fifty divided by twenty. So twenty S equals L plus one hundred fifty. Now for the second platform,
time taken equals twenty-five seconds.
S equals
L plus two hundred fifty
divided by twenty-five.
So twenty-five S equals L plus two hundred fifty. Now subtract equation one from equation two.
Twenty-five S minus twenty S equals
L plus two hundred fifty minus
L plus one hundred fifty.
The train length gets canceled automatically.
Five seconds equals one hundred seconds equals twenty meters per second. Hence, the speed of the train is twenty meter per second. So the correct option is option D.
